title: Shape and Color Analysis at Wing-Size and Wing-Pattern Levels
author: Wei-Ping Chan
materials: Inspect all specimens before running the dorsal-ventral analysis
incorrect wing grid for the right hindwing Example
Replot the visualization with customized settings
Multispectral reflectance at the wing-size level

steps.title: Prepare Segmented Images
steps.instruction: Download all images from Shape_analysis/wing_segmentation to a local folder. Ensure all images contain the suffix 'wing_segmentation.jpg'.

steps.title: Generate Specimen Preference Table
steps.instruction: Create a preference table to track specimen quality. This can be done manually or via the provided Mathematica script.

substeps.instruction: If using the script, define refdir (path to wing_segmentation directory) and outDir (path to output directory).
The script generates a CSV with columns: 'barcode', 'side', 'template', 'LF_wing_d', 'RF_wing_d', 'LH_wing_d', 'RH_wing_d', 'Body', 'L_antennae_d', 'R_antennae_d'.
Note: 'template' is a concatenation of 'barcode' and 'side' (e.g., 'MCZ-ENT000000001_dorsal').
Upload the table to Google Drive and color columns to match segmented body-part colors; default cells should be filled with 1.

steps.title: Detect Incomplete Specimens
steps.instruction: Use the provided Mathematica script to identify specimens missing either dorsal or ventral images.

substeps.instruction: Run the script against the wing_segmentation directory to find barcodes with only one side present.
Run the script against the wing_shape_matrices-seg directory to check for missing .mat files (suffix '_morph-seg.mat').

steps.title: Inspect Body Part Quality
steps.instruction: Perform a quality check of segmented images against the preference table to exclude damaged or anomalous segments.

substeps.instruction: Open the segmented images folder (e.g., using Adobe Bridge) and the Google Drive preference table side-by-side.
Change a cell value to 0 if a body part is not ideal (e.g., broken antenna, damaged wing).
Note: 'Left' and 'Right' designations are relative to the dorsal image; in ventral images, 'right' pieces appear on the left and vice versa.

steps.title: Generate Initial Wing Grids
steps.instruction: Run the dorsal-ventral mapping script on the cluster to generate wing grids.

substeps.instruction: Identify the folder containing 'morph-seg.mat' files (usually */Shape_analysis/wing_shape_matrices-seg).
Download MatLab scripts from GitHub to a MATLAB_CODE_LIBRARY.
Execute the command: batch_dorsal_ventral_mapping sbatch batch_dorsal_ventral_mapping.sh MORPH-SEG_DIR SPP_MATRICES_DIR/ MANUAL_GRID_DIR MATLAB_CODE_LIBRARY RESULT_DIR GRID_RESOLUTION
Set GRID_RESOLUTION to 5 (default) for 2^5 * 2^5 grids per wing piece.
Ensure SPP_MATRICES_DIR ends with a '/'.

steps.title: Evaluate Grid Accuracy
steps.instruction: Inspect the generated wing grids using Adobe Bridge to identify segmentation or mapping errors.

substeps.instruction: If segmentation is incorrect (e.g., overlapping wings), rerun the process from Step 6.2 of the Primary Processing Protocol.
If segmentation is correct but the grid is unideal (e.g., curved wings in jumbo specimens), move the image to a subfolder named 'manual' (manual_grid_redo_directory).

steps.title: Manually Correct Wing Grids
steps.instruction: Correct problematic grids using the 'manual_wing_grid_correction' script and 'manually_define_grid.m' in MatLab.

substeps.instruction: Download the script and verify required toolboxes via required_toolboxes.txt.
Run 'manually_define_grid.m', specifying paths to the manual_grid_redo_directory.
Use the cursor to drag red/green landmarks in clockwise order: 4 joint landmarks (red) and 4 wing corner landmarks (green).
Press ENTER to confirm a point (it will snap to the nearest edge), 'r' to redo, or 'f' to force-exit.
Upload the resulting 'spp_manual_grid_parameters' folder to the cluster.

steps.title: Finalize Wing Grids
steps.instruction: Relaunch the dorsal-ventral mapping script incorporating the manual corrections.

substeps.instruction: Run the batch_dorsal_ventral_mapping command again, this time specifying MANUAL_GRID_DIR as the 'spp_manual_grid_parameters' directory.
Download the final results from 'spp_wing_parameter' to the local disk.

steps.title: Prepare Grouping Data
steps.instruction: Create a dataset defining specimen groups for summary analysis.

substeps.instruction: Create a CSV where the first column is 'barcode' and subsequent columns are group names; fill cells with the group name if the specimen belongs to that group.
Convert this CSV to .json format using the provided Mathematica script or manually.
The resulting .json should map group names to lists of barcodes (e.g., "Lycaenidae": ["barcode1", "barcode2"]).

steps.title: Calculate Multispectral Reflectance
steps.instruction: Summarize reflectance of multispectral wavelength bands at the wing-size level.

substeps.instruction: Ensure all *AllBandsMask.mat and *morph-seg.mat files are complete in their directories.
Run the command: multispectral_wavelength_band_summary sbatch batch_BW_bands_analysis.sh SPP_MATRICES_DIR MORPH-SEG_DIR MATLAB_CODE_LIBRARY RESULT_DIR REF_THRESHOLD

Run the analysis multiple times with different REF_THRESHOLD values (customarily {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5}) to optimize signal-to-noise ratio for different bands (e.g., lower for UV, higher for 940nm).

steps.title: Generate Group Summaries and Visualizations
steps.instruction: Produce summary data and customized visualizations for the groups of interest.

substeps.instruction: In MatLab, specify paths to the preference table and group_list.json in the header of 'specimen_group_summary.m'.
Download visualization scripts from GitHub and verify toolboxes.
Run scripts and adjust parameters to find the most suitable visualization for the target group.
